headline: Keep {arm:September}: both candidates regress on character adherence and raise production cost.
lede: {arm:September} achieves the highest pass rate and lowest spend, while {arm:1017} and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} degrade character adherence without offering savings. Switching models requires a candidate that delivers measurable cost reductions or beats {arm:September} on character adherence.

slots.text: Retain {arm:September} in production. It leads on character adherence (v2) at {pass_rate.September|pct} and incurs {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k}.

{arm:1017} regresses on character adherence by {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points ({contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.interval|pts}) and adds cost. {arm:qwen3.8-flash} regresses by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points ({contrast.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character.interval|pts}) and also increases cost.

The weakest margin is {arm:qwen3.8-flash} at {weakest.value} against {weakest.threshold} on {weakest.criterion} (gap {weakest.margin}, interval {weakest.interval}). Note that {arm:1017} varied in reasoning ratio ({reasoning_ratio.1017|pct} vs {reasoning_ratio.September|pct}), and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} had two degraded harness runs totaling two dropped cells.
Test a candidate that reduces reasoning overhead without collapsing character adherence in the off lane stratum.
